plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms with golden centers. They flower in the cool, damp days of winter, when most gardens are bare. Petals can be crisp white, blushing pink or deep crimson.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, with a peak in mid-winter to early spring
plants.location: Southern Japan, the southeastern United States and mild temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, gives us tea. Camellia japonica seeds are pressed into prized camellia oil, which has long been used in Japanese hair care and cooking.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A gnarled, graceful tree that opens fragrant blossoms on bare branches, sometimes dusted with snow. Its perfume drifts through winter gardens and is one of the earliest signs of spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring, often starting in January in mild regions
plants.location: Southern and eastern China, and warmer parts of Japan
plants.funFact: In East Asian art and poetry the plum blossom stands for resilience, because it blooms in the cold before any other tree.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall stems carry round clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers above fountains of strappy leaves. The blooms are a rich blue-violet, and they brighten southern summer gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, roughly December to February
plants.location: Eastern South Africa, and gardens across Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, it isn't a true lily. Its name comes from the Greek words for 'love' and 'flower'.
